Source: http://www.scoop.co.nz

Posted July 11, 2000
(MarijuanaNews note: Educators per se are not supposed to be experts on drugs or drug laws.

They are supposed to be experts on intellectual standards, logic, the scientific method, and the other elements that equip us to live in a rapidly changing society.

Moreover, they must -- above all else -- imbue in their students a commitment to the truth. Education, especially in a time of rapid change, must be about learning how to learn. These educators do not seem to have learned even that.)

New Zealand MPs asked to reject liberalisation of drug laws
Monday, 10 July 2000
Press Release: NZ School Trustees Association
http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO0007/S00034.htm

Individual MPs asked to reject liberalisation of drug laws
See
Honest Journalism From New Zealand Tries to Deal With the Questions About Legalization That Apply Everywhere.
and
California Bureaucracy Suppresses Report Showing Marijuana Use Among California Students Leveled Off After Passage Of Prop 215. Meanwhile, In New Zealand, Prohbitionists Use The Same Party Line. 2 Items
and links

A group representing 12 key educational organisations is so concerned about the moves to decriminalise cannabis, that it has written to every Member of Parliament asking them to reject any change.

The group, called The Education Accord, is made up of the leaders of the 12 key educational organisations, including unions, principals, Maori and trustees. It has sent MPs a unanimous statement on the issue expressing its concerns.

NZSTA President Owen Edgerton says the group collectively has considerable experience working in and with schools and students and is very worried about the effects decriminalisation will have on teenagers.
(MarijuanaNews note: Their stated area of expertise is not social policy, and while it is appropriate that they are concerned about " teenagers, " one need not be an " educator " to be concerned about children.

In any case, it does not follow that changing the laws on marijuana use by adults will result in a higher rate of marijuana – by either adults or children. New Zealand has a much higher rate of teen marijuana use than Holland. )

In the statement, the Accord says it is important that all Members of Parliament are fully aware of the harm that cannabis causes to children and adolescents.

" Cannabis causes physiological damage to developing organs. It also results in " emotional stunting " as cannabis causes blockages of the neural pathways, impeding users’ ability to exercise reason and sound judgement, " it says.
(MarijuanaNews note: There is not the slightest bit of evidence to support these claims. It would be ethically impossible to do controlled studies to determine if they were true.

However, it would be possible to study teens who have used a large amount of marijuana, and compare them with those who have not used any. Where is this data? There is none.

Moreover, given the huge number of New Zealand teens who have used cannabis, if this were true, then a large segment of the New Zealand population would show these dire long-term consequences. Where are the bodies?
See
Reefer Madness in New Zealand Op-ed Says " We Are Killing Our Kids With Cannabis'. " And A Little Prohibitionist Humor.

This is not to say that heavy marijuana use does not involve any risk for teens. Adolescents who are heavy marijuana users tend to have more problems than those who do not. Of course, correlation is not causation. Marijuana use may be a symptom, not a cause of the problems.

But would these problems become worse if marijuana were decriminalized or legalized? Perhaps these problems would actually be easier to handle – without marijuana prohibition.)

" The educational achievement of children and adolescents who use cannabis is severely compromised due to the physiological and emotional side effects of this usage. "
(MarijuanaNews note: Notice that this statement would apply to all users. Children know that this is not true – from their own observations. See the item from Ireland below.)

The Education Accord is already concerned about the current level of cannabis taking among young people, and believes that decriminalisation will result in increased use within that age group.
(MarijuanaNews note: New Zealand has a much higher rate of marijuana use than Holland, which should have the highest rate of marijuana use in the world if the " educationalist’s " premise were correct.)
See
Chairman of The Youth Trust of New Zealand Parrots DEAland Lies About Dutch. Whom Can Youth Trust?

It is concerned that it will lead to higher levels of violence and ill-health in our society.
(MarijuanaNews note: Violence? Ill health?)
See
The Dutch Demonstrate Common Sense, and the Canadians – Even the Police – Seem Ready to Learn – 3 Articles
and
Great London Times Column and News From New Zealand Compare Marijuana and Alcohol

The educationalists say that instead of liberalising the laws, they urge MPs to support the provision of more effective support services for users and their families, and for an effective education programme in schools, available for students from year 1 to year 13.
(MarijuanaNews note: " Education " based on the above statement would be counterproductive. The children of New Zealand deserve better from the educationalist establishment. Clearly, there is a need for educational reform.)

From The Irish Times
lettersed@irish-times.ie

By Joe Humphreys

YOUTH COUNCIL CONDEMNS `SCARE TACTICS' ON DRUGS
Excerpt:

The use of " scare tactics " in public information campaigns on drugs is ineffective and possibly counter-productive, the National Youth Council of Ireland has said.

In a submission to the National Drugs Strategy review committee, the youth organisation said such tactics did not " respect their target audience and have been shown to be at such variance to young people's own knowledge and experience as to render them useless ".
